research_question: Among children with otitis media with effusion (OME), what is the effect of intranasal corticosteroids, with or without co-treatments administered equally in both eligible arms, versus no intranasal steroid treatment (no treatment or the same co-treatment alone) on persistence of middle ear effusion at the first assessment up to 1 month (operationally ≤6 weeks) after treatment initiation?
treatment_label: Intranasal corticosteroid (e.g., mometasone, beclomethasone, budesonide, or fluticasone), with any co-treatment given equally to both arms
control_label: No intranasal steroid treatment (no treatment or the same co-treatment alone), excluding placebo nasal spray controls
outcome_description: Dichotomous persistence of OME at the first post-baseline assessment occurring no later than 6 weeks after treatment initiation, extracted as events and total participants per arm. Persistence includes effusion still present, type-B tympanogram, type-C2 or non-type-A tympanogram when defined by the study as failure, not cured, no improvement, or persistent effusion. Resolution/cure includes type-A tympanogram or complete clearance; when only resolution or improvement counts are reported, derive persistence as total minus resolved. For ordinal or multi-category headline outcomes, seek post-treatment tympanogram or cure/no-cure tables and derive persistence rather than discarding the study. Prefer child-level data; if only ear-level data are available, sum events and totals across right and left ears and never select one ear alone. Do not include hearing thresholds or air-bone gap, symptoms or parent-reported improvement, quality of life, adverse events, or outcomes measured after 6 weeks.
positive_direction: A positive Hedges g, if a standardized effect is displayed, means less persistent middle ear effusion and therefore favors intranasal steroids; for the prespecified pooled risk ratio, RR below 1 favors intranasal steroids.

inclusion_criteria: Original empirical studies of children with OME that compare an intranasal corticosteroid regimen with an eligible no-steroid condition; co-treatments are permitted when administered equally to the compared arms.

Studies reporting quantitative information on persistence, resolution, cure, improvement, or post-treatment tympanogram categories from which persistent effusion event counts and arm totals can be obtained or derived at a first assessment no later than 6 weeks.
Studies reporting outcomes per child or per ear; ear-level studies are eligible when data for both ears can be combined.
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study, including systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, opinion pieces, and theoretical papers.

No comparison between an intranasal-steroid treatment condition and an eligible no-steroid control condition receiving no treatment or the same co-treatment; also exclude oral/systemic steroid comparisons, placebo nasal-spray controls, and unmatched active-treatment arms.

No quantitative outcome data capable of producing an effect size—specifically, no usable event counts and totals, means with SDs, t/F statistics, proportions, or odds ratios—and persistence counts cannot be derived from resolution, cure, improvement, or tympanogram data.

Completely unrelated to pediatric OME or reporting only ineligible outcomes/time points, such as hearing thresholds or air-bone gap, symptoms or parent-reported improvement, quality of life, adverse events, or assessments after 6 weeks.
moderators_to_extract: Use and type of equally administered co-treatment
Timing of the eligible follow-up assessment
effect_size_note: Pool study-level risk ratios using a random-effects model. Define the event as persistent effusion, so RR < 1 favors intranasal steroids. Extract events and totals for steroid and control arms; convert resolution/cure to persistence by subtracting resolved cases from the relevant total. For ear-level reporting, sum right- and left-ear events and totals and do not use one ear alone. In multi-arm trials, retain only the intranasal-steroid arm and the no-steroid arm with the same co-treatment, ignoring oral-steroid, montelukast, antihistamine-only, and other active arms. Use the first eligible assessment at ≤6 weeks. Document effect estimator, random-effects method, confidence intervals, heterogeneity (tau-squared and I-squared), and sensitivity analyses for child- versus ear-level data and alternative persistence definitions where feasible.
single_outcome_target: persistence of otitis media with effusion
